conventions.ref: "<FILE>:<type>:<name>". FILE is MAIN (TEST_MAIN) or EXT (TEST_EXT); type is the parser's ObjectType. Fields are "Table::field". Relationships use the parser's label "LeftTO → RightTO" and match in either direction.
conventions.descendants: A ref ending in "/**" means the object or anything contained in it (parentUid chain): a layout and its layout objects, a custom menu and its items.
conventions.targets: "to" is a resolved ref; "broken:<type>" is a reference whose target was deleted (broken: true); "unresolved:<type>" is a target that can't be verified (not broken, not resolved). "broken:field|tableOccurrence" accepts either type.
conventions.edge: { to, kind?, via?, step?, disabled? }. kind, via and step are checked only when given. via is the table occurrence a field edge reads through. step is the 1-based script step index (fromStep).
conventions.exact: exact: true means the source's outbound edges must equal the listed set (nothing missing, nothing extra). exact: false means the listed edges must exist; extras are allowed.
conventions.unverified: A string explaining why FileMaker's XML for this case hasn't been observed yet. A mismatch there is a question to investigate first, not automatically a parser bug.
conventions.matchers: Attribute values: a plain string must match exactly; {"contains": s} is a substring match; {"oneOf": [..]} matches any; {"absent": true} means the attribute must not be set; {"present": true} means it must be set.
conventions.ignoredTypes: Object types listed in ignoredTypes aren't checked: edges to them are neither required nor flagged as extra, and they're left out of the unreferenced and unused-chain checks.
